title: Three known CHIME dispersion trends pass a daily test, but only one passes two 30-day block checks in a 13-source screen
abstract: We test linear dispersion-measure changes in 13 CHIME/FRB Catalog 2 repeaters with at least ten accepted observing days across 180 days. Equal-day fits and controls for peak frequency and pulse width retain three known trends after a 13-source correction. Their adjusted slopes are +1.026, -1.291, and +1.415 pc cm^-3 yr^-1 for FRB 20190117A, FRB 20220529A, and FRB 20220912A. Only FRB 20190117A passes both exploratory 30-day block tests; none of the three passes both 90-day block tests. A comparison with 1076 independent FAST records yields ten shared dates. Their CHIME-minus-FAST slope interval includes zero. Thus, the data do not establish a telescope discrepancy or a new plasma signal. Small samples, uncertain temporal dependence, and burst morphology limit physical inference. The package includes frozen inputs, exact source hashes, code, all source tests, controls, simulations, figures, and offline instructions.
